stem: During developmental surveillance, which birth history item should the clinician specifically ask about?

options.text: Maternal factors such as gestational diabetes, smoking, or alcohol exposure
The child’s current screen time only
The number of siblings in the household only

explanation: Maternal factors such as gestational diabetes, smoking, or alcohol exposure are relevant birth history details to ask about during developmental surveillance.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Page 94

optionExplanations.A: Correct because maternal factors including gestational diabetes, smoking, and alcohol exposure are explicitly relevant components of the birth history.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because a parent’s preferred school subjects are not part of the birth history.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because current screen time is not a birth history item.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because the number of siblings is not a specific birth history detail being targeted here.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because the family’s holiday plans are unrelated to birth history.
